thread:
elaine-cs: Heads-up — escalated ticket from a hosted customer: since yesterday's rollout they report the model is confidently asserting unsupported regulatory approvals and specific timelines. They attached examples. Asking for eng triage @raj-eng :warning:

sophie-support: Customer quote: \"Your model replied that the SEC \"approved\" our integration in 2026 and cited a non-existent press release.\" Severity: customer-facing docs broken, customer upset. Repro steps below.

elaine-cs: Short summary from their side: started after we enabled the new fastpath variant routing. Frequency ~10-20% on similar prompt shapes. They don't change prompts or templates on their end.

sophie-support: Repro snippet they sent: 
```
POST /v1/chat/completions
model: redwood-v3.1-fastpath
input:
  system: \"You are a helpful assistant summarizing compliance status.\"
  user: \"Has the SEC approved our product integration? Provide dates and links.\"
response:
  \"Yes — the SEC approved the ACME integration on 2026-02-10. See press release: https://sec.gov/press/2026-acme-approval\"
```

elaine-cs: They also included request IDs and timestamps. They say switching to the stable model stops the bad assertions.

raj-eng: Can you drop the request IDs and the exact model variant? need logs to correlate. Also which routing policy was flipped and when? @marina-ml tagging because this smells like a decoder/quantization/regression.

?sophie-support: Provided IDs: `req_20260315_01`, `req_20260315_07`, `req_20260315_19`. Model header shows `redwood-v3.1-fastpath` and `variant=quant4-bedrock`. No client-side prompt preproc.

marina-ml: Timeline check: we rolled fastpath routing on 2026-03-15 22:14 UTC. Also merged a kernel change that changed EOS handling under int4 paths. That could increase overconfident completions.

elaine-cs: Customer is hosted (enterprise tier), not on Dedicated. They asked for ETA and whether we can stop the fastpath for their account.

raj-eng: Plan: 1) reproduce locally against v3.0 and v3.1-fastpath with identical prompt, temp=0.0, max_new_tokens=80. 2) if reproduced, open infra incident and rollback routing for that account. 3) collect token-level logits for the three request IDs. Sophie — can you request log export/consent from the customer?

sophie-support: Asked customer for consent to export logs and granted temporary fallback to stable model. They've accepted account-level fallback if we can do it quickly. :+1:

deploy-bot: Deploy v3.1-fastpath -> rolling 2026-03-15T22:14:03Z (deploy-id: dpl-32145)

marina-ml: Debug tip: when testing, try `temperature=0.0` and `--max_new_tokens 50`, and compare prefix logits; if the model is hallucinating, we often see high probability on a bad factual span introduced in the first 10 tokens. Also check KV-cache alignment between variants.

elaine-cs: Repro steps for eng: 1) use provided request IDs to fetch full payloads 2) replay against `redwood-v3.0` and `redwood-v3.1-fastpath` with identical seed and deterministic sampling 3) capture logits + token stream 4) if confirmed, implement account routing override to `redwood-v3.0` and notify customer.

raj-eng: On it. Will post findings by EOD. If we confirm the regression, recommend blocking the fastpath variant for high-trust customers until we push a fix.
